# The seeded defect catalogue

Each defect is a realistic way to build the demo connector wrong, introduced by swapping one
part of its composition (see `demo/src/acme_mail_mcp/defects.py`). Start the connector with
`ACME_MCP_DEFECTS=<id>` to reproduce any of them. Which layer actually catches each one is
measured, not asserted: see [the defect matrix](defect-matrix.md).

| Defect | Expected layer | What breaks | Where this happens for real |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `schema-invalid-type` | 1 | max_results is published as {"type": "int"}, which no validator accepts. | A schema written by hand, or ported from another language's type names. |
| `bind-all-interfaces` | 1 | The SDK enables Origin validation only for localhost binds; on 0.0.0.0 it is off. | Containerising a server: the bind address changes, and the defaults change with it. |
| `nondeterministic-tool-order` | 1 | Tools are published in a per-process random order, so no client can cache the list. | Registering tools from a set, or from unordered plugin discovery. |
| `blocking-event-loop` | 1 | One slow search freezes every other request on the connection. | A sync HTTP client left inside an async handler. |
| `readonly-get-marks-read` | 2 | get_message fetches without peek, so reading mutates the mailbox. | IMAP's BODY[] instead of BODY.PEEK[] — the classic silent mutation. |
| `trash-not-destructive` | 2 | trash_message declares destructiveHint=false, so clients skip the confirmation. | Annotations copied from a neighbouring tool and never revisited. |
| `send-marked-idempotent` | 2 | send_message declares idempotentHint=true, inviting clients to retry it. | Idempotency treated as a property of the code path rather than of the effect. |
| `optional-param-required` | 2 | label is optional in inputSchema but rejected as missing at call time. | Hand-written validation that drifted from the generated schema. |
| `output-schema-drift` | 2 | received_at is published as an integer while the connector sends RFC 3339 text. | A schema edited by hand after the serializer changed. |
| `cache-key-missing-tenant` | 3 | One tenant's search results are served to another. | A cache added for latency, keyed by the query that was easy to reach. |
| `token-in-error-message` | 3 | Upstream failures carry the Authorization header into tool results and logs. | Debug context added during an incident and never removed. |
| `no-token-refresh` | 3 | Every tool call fails once the upstream access token expires mid-session. | Refresh implemented at login only, never on the request path. |
| `accepts-foreign-audience` | 3 | An upstream credential is accepted as proof of identity by the MCP endpoint. | The antipattern the MCP authorization spec names explicitly. |
| `pagination-first-page-only` | 4 | Results are silently truncated at the provider's page cap. | Pagination tested on a small mailbox, shipped against a large one. |
| `ignores-retry-after` | 4 | The connector hammers the provider instead of waiting the requested interval. | A retry loop written before anyone read the rate-limit documentation. |
| `retries-send-on-timeout` | 4 | An ambiguous failure becomes a duplicate email. | One retry policy applied to every verb. |
| `timezone-offset-dropped` | 4 | received_at is truncated to a naive string, moving late-evening mail to another day. | Dates 'normalised' on the way through a connector. |
| `drift-returns-nulls` | 4 | A renamed upstream field turns into an empty subject rather than an error. | Defensive .get() calls that hide a provider's v2 rollout. |
| `unbounded-body` | 4 | A multi-megabyte message is handed to the model in full. | Budgets that exist in the design document and nowhere else. |
| `vague-tool-descriptions` | 5 | Every tool is described as 'Mail operation.', so the model has to guess. | Descriptions trimmed to save tokens. |
| `untrusted-content-unmarked` | 5 | Nothing tells the model that a message body is text written by a stranger. | Tool output treated as data the model can trust. |

## One defect that is not here

A stray `print()` that corrupts the stdio stream is the most common stdio bug in the wild, and
it cannot be seeded into this connector: while the Python SDK's `stdio_server()` is serving, it
points file descriptor 1 at stderr and keeps the protocol stream on a private descriptor, so
handler output never reaches the wire. The check for it (P-014) is still in the kit — servers
built on other SDKs, or on none, are not protected — and the fixture server proves it fires.
